chapter: Three Deuces and 52nd Street with Tatum
title: Learning from the radio; resemblance to Charlie Christian
summary: He learned everything from the radio and says he already played in Christian's vein before hearing him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did you ever copy things off of records?
No, I didn't have a record machine. I just never had no record machine for a long, --- It came from the radio, everything I learned, radio.
People have said you sounded a lot like Charlie Christian.

He was a big influence. Because the things that he played I had in mind to play a long time. That's the way I wanted -- before I even heard him. It wasn't a matter of copying. It was a matter of -- I'd have to associate it with Ross Columbo and Bing Crosby. They both sounded alike. So it wasn't a matter of somebody copying somebody. --- A lot of people sound alike. Just like a lot of people fares no kin, but they look alike -- look like they come from the same family. So, it wasn't a matter of me copying, I mean the things he played, if you notice, there is not that many of his riffs, it's just the sound, and the style. Not that many of his riffs on none of my records. Some of the things I have played, Soft Winds I played --- Profamelly Blue. But I mean 90% overall you don't find me doing his riffs. You'll hear maybe now and then. But the sound, we sounded alike. I didn't copy him. If I was copying him I could have never did it that quick. --- It just come natural. --- We just happened to think that way. That's the way I look at it.
